cases.persona: Ada, 24 payments, a mild low month (invented, FIN-22)
cases.situation: Ada's pay came in at $2,700 instead of $3,000 in September; every other month brought $3,000. She looks at a $2,400 sofa on 24 monthly payments at 0%, first payment on 15 December. She also has $4,000 in a savings account. A usual month: pay $3,000, bills $1,500 and everyday spending $900 ($600 of it on essentials), so it leaves $600. Her everyday account holds $1,050 on 15 November 2026 (today); nothing is saved in a safety net.
cases.why: Payments are $2,400 / 24 = $100 a month. A usual month leaves $600 - $100 = $500. Her low month (September) leaves $2,700 - $1,500 - $900 = $300, and $300 - $100 = $200, so even the low month carries the payment over the whole 24 months: no low-month caution and no savings bridge. The answer is "Fits"; with nothing saved in a safety net it carries the no-net caution (no_net), as every fit does today. This month is unchanged ($600 left after the plan, first payment in December).
cases.plannerNote: Engine today gives exactly this answer (06.1-30 probe, 2026-11-12). The drafted FIN-22 rule adds nothing here.

cases.persona: Ada, 24 payments, the low month falls short, savings carry it (invented, FIN-22)
cases.situation: Ada's records show 1 low month in the last 6: September, when $1,500 came in. She looks at a $4,800 sofa on 24 monthly payments at 0%, first payment on 15 December. $4,000 is in her savings account (not marked as a safety net). A usual month: pay $3,000, bills $1,500 and everyday spending $900 ($600 of it on essentials), so it leaves $600. Her everyday account holds $1,050 on 15 November 2026 (today); nothing is saved in a safety net.
cases.why: Payments are $4,800 / 24 = $200 a month. A usual month leaves $600 - $200 = $400. A month like September leaves $1,500 - $2,400 = -$900, so it is $900 + $200 = $1,100 short with the payment. 1 low month in 6 means about 24 / 6 = 4 low months over the 24 payments (to November 2028), about 4 x $1,100 = $4,400 in all. The usual months between them leave $400 each, so savings only need to hold one low month at a time ($1,100), and she has $4,000. The answer is "Fits, a low month is tight" (low_month), with the lines "Judged against a low month like September, which leaves about -$900." and "In a month like September, about $1,100 would come from savings. Over 24 payments, to November 2028, that could happen about 4 times. That is about $4,400 of your $4,000." (see the open question on that last sentence).
cases.plannerNote: Engine today gives exactly this answer (06.1-30 probe). The low-month check already runs over the whole term (FIN-08, 05.4-23): the count of low months grows with the length of the plan.

cases.persona: Ada, a 60-month car loan at 7.9% (invented, FIN-22)
cases.situation: Same Ada and savings as LL-02 (1 low month in 6, September at $1,500, $4,000 saved). She looks at a $15,000 car on 60 monthly payments at 7.9%, first payment on 15 December. A usual month: pay $3,000, bills $1,500 and everyday spending $900 ($600 of it on essentials), so it leaves $600. Her everyday account holds $1,050 on 15 November 2026 (today); nothing is saved in a safety net.
cases.why: Payments are $303.43 a month: $15,000 at 7.9% over 60 months, rounded up to the cent. Over the loan she pays $18,205.71, so $3,205.71 is interest, 21% of the amount, over the 10% line: borrowing costs a lot, so the answer is "Fits only by borrowing" (fits_by_borrowing), and that code has no low-month row. A usual month leaves $600 - $303.43 = $296.57. A month like September is $900 + $303.43 = $1,203.43 short with the payment, about 60 / 6 = 10 times over the 60 payments (to November 2031), $12,034.30 in all; the usual months between leave $296.57 each, so savings need to hold one low month at a time ($1,203.43 of her $4,000). The low-month lines still show on the borrowing answer: "Judged against a low month like September, which leaves about -$900." and "In a month like September, about $1,203.43 would come from savings. Over 60 payments, to November 2031, that could happen about 10 times. That is about $12,034.30 of your $4,000."
cases.plannerNote: Engine today gives exactly this answer. The plan's drafted fallback fact (long_plan_low_month, for a code with no low-month row) would repeat lean_bridge here; see the open questions.

She looks at a $7,200 sofa on 36 monthly payments at 0%, first payment on 15 December. $4,000 is in her savings account. Her everyday account holds $1,050 on 15 November 2026 (today); nothing is saved in a safety net.
cases.why: Payments are $7,200 / 36 = $200 a month; a usual month leaves $600 - $200 = $400. No month in her records is lower than the usual one, so there is no low month to check the long plan against: the answer is "Fits" with the no-net caution, no low-month lines.

cases.persona: Ada, 24 payments, the low month falls short and nothing is saved (invented, FIN-22)
cases.situation: Same Ada and sofa as LL-02 (1 low month in 6, September at $1,500; $4,800 on 24 monthly payments at 0%), but she has no savings account. A usual month: pay $3,000, bills $1,500 and everyday spending $900 ($600 of it on essentials), so it leaves $600. Her everyday account holds $1,050 on 15 November 2026 (today); nothing is saved in a safety net.
cases.why: A usual month carries the $200 payment ($400 left), but a month like September is $1,100 short with it, about 4 times over the 24 payments, and nothing is saved to carry one. The records alone cannot say it fits, so the answer asks: "Can you cover $200 a month for 24 months, even in your low months?"
